anomaly_def.Name: Optimizer Statistics Anomaly + MVCC Version Maintenance Anomaly + Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Optimizer Statistics Anomaly : Stale, missing, or incomplete optimizer statistics cause systematic misestimation of predicate selectivity and cardinalities, leading the planner to choose sub-optimal access paths and join orders.
MVCC Version Maintenance Anomaly : Excess accumulation of obsolete row versions and index entries causes table and index bloat, heavier visibility checks, and persistent background-cleanup pressure in a high-churn OLTP system.
Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly : Insufficient or congested network and connection-handling capacity limits the rate at which clients can establish sessions or transfer result sets, creating connection backlogs and socket-level waits.

When all three defects co-exist, the database exhibits a blend of execution-plan instability, growing on-disk and in-memory footprints, and erratic end-to-end latency. Misestimated plans may trigger full-table scans or inefficient nested loops that read vast swaths of bloated heaps; the extra I/O magnifies MVCC-induced scan times because more dead tuples must be skipped. Long-running queries inflate the number of concurrent backends holding snapshots, slowing version cleanup even further. As heap and index sizes swell, the optimizer’s already stale statistics become progressively less representative, compounding estimation errors. Concurrently, enlarged result sets generated by sub-optimal plans congest outbound network buffers, while prolonged query runtimes keep connections open, exhausting listener slots and causing connection attempts to time out. Clients observe sporadic spikes in response times, query cancellations, and authentication failures, while DBAs see divergent estimated vs. actual rows, rising autovacuum lag, blazing version-store growth, swelling relation sizes, and OS socket queues overflowing.

Causally, MVCC bloat inflates table size and skews data distribution, which degrades the accuracy of existing statistics; the optimizer therefore chooses plans that scan or join far more data than anticipated, lengthening query execution. The longer queries run, the longer snapshots stay alive, delaying version reclamation and accelerating version-store growth—a positive feedback loop. The heavier I/O and CPU demand further slows background cleanup workers, letting bloat expand. Meanwhile, the oversized result sets and extended query durations hold server processes and network sockets, pushing connection pools and listener queues to their limits. Connection contention triggers client retries, amplifying network load and session churn, which in turn increases transaction open/close activity and further burdens MVCC bookkeeping. The intertwined effects of poor statistics, MVCC bloat, and network saturation thus reinforce each other, driving the system into a deteriorating performance spiral.

entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with connection establishment, authentication exchange, protocol correctness, network reachability, or client/server communication stability.
entry.solution_guidance: Check endpoint reachability, authentication flow, connection limits, protocol compatibility, transport stability, and client connection lifecycle management.
